title: Migrate interaction tokens to theme variable layer and resolve hover glow regression
creator: Maya Torres
description:
Summary: Migrate all interactive state colors and elevation effects (hover, focus, active, disabled, pressed, and loading overlays) from component-local tokens into the new theme variable layer so they resolve consistently across light/dark/high-contrast themes. While doing this migration, fix a visible hover 'glow' regression that appears on icon-only and compact buttons when motion is reduced and when both inner and outer shadows are applied.

Background: During the tokens consolidation in Q4 we introduced per-component state tokens for buttons to support rapid experiments. Those tokens diverged from the theme layer and produced inconsistent hover/active treatments in some combinations: dark theme + high-contrast + reduced-motion. A recent customer bug report surfaced a flicker/glow where stacked shadows briefly show as double outlines on icon-only buttons when moving the pointer or programmatically toggling loading state.

Goal: Ensure all button interactive states are sourced from theme variables (not component-level overrides), eliminate the stacking shadow/glow regression, and add automated visual/interaction tests to catch regressions across themes and motion preferences. Deliverables: token migration PR, Figma token update, updated component docs, automated Cypress+Percy snapshots, accessibility signoff.

Out of scope: Rewriting button anatomy or changing visual language beyond aligning existing tokens to the theme; any JS runtime batching of hover events (handled by runtime team).
acceptance_criteria: All button variants (primary, secondary, ghost, destructive, link, icon-only, compact) read hover/focus/active/disabled/loading colors and shadow values from theme variables
No visual difference in baseline appearance after migration for default theme; intended fixes only resolve the hover/glow regression
Hover glow regression reproduced in a test harness before the fix and verified resolved after changes in light/dark/high-contrast
Reduced-motion preference preserves semantics (no new motion introduced) and no double-shadow artifacts
Figma token set updated and cross-checked with the new theme variables; figma link added to PR
Unit/visual tests added: component-level storyshots and e2e visual snapshots across themes and reduced-motion
Design documentation updated with migration notes, reasoning, and a short troubleshooting section for future regressions
comments: 2026-02-16 - Maya Torres: Filed after a customer reported double outline on icon buttons in high-contrast. Attached initial screenshots and minimal repro steps.

2026-02-20 - Evan Gupta: Confirmed repro locally. Root cause appears to be overlapping CSS box-shadows: one from the component hover token and one from an outer focus ring variable. Proposed approach: move both to theme variables and dedupe by expressing focus as outline rather than stacked shadow for compact/icon buttons.
2026-02-25 - PM review (Jordan Lee): OK to proceed with migration; prioritize preserving backwards visual parity. Blocked on Figma token naming convention finalization.
2026-03-02 - DesignOps (Rina Patel): Figma tokens approved. Added mapping table in Confluence. Link provided in design_links.
2026-03-04 - Evan Gupta: Opened WIP PR with token mapping and three component updates (primary, icon-only, compact). Included visual snapshots. Not all contrast cases green yet in Percy.

2026-03-07 - Accessibility review (Samir Khan): Verified reduced-motion behavior. Noted a keyboard focus visibility regression for ghost variant when focus ring switched from shadow to outline; requested a variant fallback to maintain 3px minimum visible focus in high-contrast. Adding follow-up task.

2026-03-09 - Evan Gupta: Addressed a11y note by adding a high-contrast focus color token and ensuring focus outline thickness using border-image technique for extreme scale. Percy snapshots now match baseline except for one dark-theme compact icon case (still investigating).
2026-03-10 - Maya Torres: Design review passed for the changed focus treatment. Moving ticket to In Progress -> aiming to merge by 2026-03-12 after final visual fix.
